<p class="mr-eyebrow">Why marrow</p>
<h2 class="mr-section-title">What you get</h2>

<div class="mr-grid column-page">
  <div class="mr-card">
    <span class="mr-ico">🧱</span>
    <h3>Full columnar type system</h3>
    <p>Primitive, string, binary, list, fixed-size list, struct, dictionary,
    temporal and decimal arrays — laid out exactly to the Arrow spec, with a
    separate validity bitmap for nulls.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="mr-card">
    <span class="mr-ico">⚡</span>
    <h3>SIMD compute kernels</h3>
    <p>Arithmetic, comparisons, aggregates, group-by, sorting, filtering,
    casting and hashing — vectorized and null-aware, with the same three-valued
    logic as SQL.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="mr-card">
    <span class="mr-ico">🎮</span>
    <h3>GPU-capable kernels</h3>
    <p>Element-wise arithmetic, comparison and hashing kernels can dispatch to
    Metal or CUDA through an <code>ExecContext</code> — experimental, and
    sharing the exact CPU code path.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="mr-card">
    <span class="mr-ico">🔗</span>
    <h3>Zero-copy interop</h3>
    <p>The Arrow C Data Interface means marrow arrays cross into PyArrow,
    DataFusion and Polars as pointer exchanges — no serialization, no copies.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="mr-card">
    <span class="mr-ico">🧮</span>
    <h3>Relational query layer</h3>
    <p>Build lazy plans — filter, project, aggregate, join, Parquet scan — that a
    planner compiles into a pull-based streaming executor over record batches.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="mr-card">
    <span class="mr-ico">🐍</span>
    <h3>A familiar Python API</h3>
    <p><code>import marrow as ma</code> and reach for the PyArrow names you
    already know — <code>array</code>, <code>record_batch</code>, <code>table</code>,
    <code>sort</code>, <code>filter</code>, <code>join</code>.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="mr-card">
    <span class="mr-ico">💾</span>
    <h3>Native Parquet &amp; Arrow IPC</h3>
    <p>A from-scratch Parquet reader and writer — snappy/zstd/lz4, statistics,
    page index and bloom filters, no PyArrow at runtime — plus Arrow IPC file
    and stream round-trips.</p>
  </div>
</div>

<p class="mr-eyebrow">See it in action</p>
<h2 class="mr-section-title">Sixty seconds with marrow</h2>

```{python}
#| echo: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../python")
import marrow as ma
```

Build arrays straight from Python data — the type is inferred in a single pass,
and `None` marks a null:

```{python}
ages   = ma.array([25, 35, 45, None, 55])
names  = ma.array(["Alice", "Bob", "Carol", "Dave", "Eve"])
salary = ma.array([70_000, 90_000, 110_000, 50_000, 130_000])

print(ages)
print(names)
```

Compute is vectorized and null-aware — a null in either operand propagates,
and aggregates skip nulls:

```{python}
next_year = ma.add(ages, ma.array([1, 1, 1, 1, 1]))
print("age next year:", next_year)   # index 3 stays null
print("total payroll:", ma.sum(salary))
```

Assemble columns into a `RecordBatch`, then sort and reshape it with a
PyArrow-shaped API:

```{python}
people = ma.record_batch({"age": ages, "name": names, "salary": salary})

senior = people.sort_by([("salary", "descending")])
print(senior.to_pylist())
```

Every array speaks the Arrow C Data Interface, so it round-trips through the
rest of the ecosystem with zero copies:

```{python}
#| eval: false
import pyarrow as pa
pa_table = pa.record_batch(people)     # marrow → PyArrow, no copy
back     = ma.record_batch(pa_table)   # PyArrow → marrow, no copy
```
